these poems during S.’s lifetime, and, with three exceptions (The keen stars were twinkling,
Bright wanderer, fair coquette of Heaven, and That moment is gone for ever) for many years
after his death. Most of the poems to or about Jane were given by S. to Jane or to Edward
and Jane jointly in very carefully written fair copies, which remained in Jane’s possession
at the time of S.’s death. Only a very few scraps of preparatory draft for any of these poems
survive, further confirming that S. was scrupulous in preserving them from Mary’s knowl-
edge. A curious exception is the MS from which Mary derived the poem published in 1824
as The Pine Forest of the Cascine, near Pisa (Longman vi, no. 431/432 Appendix).
